🌍 Lebanese speaker warns of ‘sedition’ after framework agreement with Israeli regime

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri issues a statement on Saturday warning nation against falling into “Fitna” following framework agreement signed under US mediation

Berri warned of the consequences of a framework agreement signed between the Lebanese government and the Israeli regime under US mediation, urging Lebanese citizens to avoid being drawn into what he called a Fitna, which roughly means sedition.
​
The statement, reported Saturday the Al-Ahed news website, was issued shortly after the deal’s signing.
​
In the brief statement addressed to the Lebanese people, Berri said: “O people of Lebanon, all of Lebanon; this is sedition.”
​
He quoted Imam Ali (AS) from Nahj al-Balagha, urging the people to be like “Ibn al-Laboun” (a two-year-old camel), “neither having a back to ride nor udders to milk”, from a well-known metaphor in Arab culture for avoiding any stance or action that could be exploited to fuel division.
​
Without elaborating further, Berri warned about the situation ahead and the potential consequences of the agreement.
​
The warning follows five rounds of negotiations and four days of talks in Washington, where Lebanon and the Israeli regime reached a framework for a future agreement on Friday under US mediation.
​
The framework was signed in the presence of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Lebanese Ambassador to the United States Nada Hamade Moawad, and Israeli regime’s ambassador to Washington Yechiel Leiter.
​
According to a report by the American news outlet Axios, the agreement outlines the path for future negotiations between the two sides and includes initial implementation steps.
​
Citing an Israeli official, the outlet reported that under the agreement, the Israeli regime will maintain its presence in the so-called “Yellow Line” security zone until Hezbollah is disarmed.

The boldest experiment in crypto

Michael Saylor, the founder of Strategy, the world's largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, has come up with something unique.

Instead of simply buying Bitcoin with the company's own money, he's building an entire financial machine that attracts outside capital and channels it into BTC purchases.

One of these instruments is STRC. Investors provide capital to the company and receive regular payouts of around 11.5% annually. The company then uses that capital to buy Bitcoin. But there's a catch.

⚙️ How it’s supposed to work

STRC — an instrument Saylor designed with the help of AI — is intended to keep its price hovering around $100.

If the price falls, the company raises the yield to attract more buyers. The price is supposed to recover. Think of it as an automatic stabilizer.

❓ Why this is interesting 

Right now, STRC is trading at roughly $83, despite its $100 target value. The yield has already been increased, but the market isn't responding the way the model was designed to.

This is the first real stress test of the entire structure. If the mechanism fails to stabilize the price, the company will either have to keep increasing payouts to investors or buy less Bitcoin.

Saylor is essentially testing one question: can financial instruments be built around a single asset indefinitely?

I recently stumbled upon something deeply unsettling.  

Bill Gates poured a massive $55 MILLION into BioNTech—the company behind the Pfizer mRNA injection.  

And you won’t believe when this investment actually happened…  

Could it really be a coincidence?  

This is the same company that teamed up with Pfizer to develop their mRNA COVID vaccine—a move that powered Pfizer’s revenue to a record-breaking $100 billion in 2022.  

So I dug a little deeper. When exactly did Gates make this significant investment?  

It was on September 4, 2019.  

Covid first came into public view just two months later, in November 2019.  

That timing turned out to be incredibly profitable. Gates’ $55 million stake reportedly surged tenfold, reaching over $550 million in just a few years.  

According to BioNTech’s press release, the funding was for “the identification of potential HIV and tuberculosis vaccine and immunotherapy candidates and their pre-clinical development.” It also helped BioNTech expand its infectious disease infrastructure and platform technology.  

Interesting.  

But here’s another twist: Bill Gates has donated around $20 million to the BBC.  

Now, reports suggest the BBC exaggerated the dangers of Covid to increase public backing for strict lockdowns.  

In other words, mainstream outlets may have misled the public, stoking fear to push support for sweeping restrictions—and possibly driving people to rush into taking the newly developed mRNA injections.  

Meanwhile, Gates’ investment kept multiplying…  

As Professor Mark Woolhouse pointed out: “One example is that they gave the impression that hospitals were being overwhelmed during the first wave. Some (mainly in London) were, but overall hospital bed occupancy was at an all-time low during that period.”  

Remember when we were constantly told hospitals were near collapse? Remember the viral TikTok videos of nurses dancing in celebration? And how anyone questioning the narrative was instantly labeled a “conspiracy theorist”?  

Turns out, those so-called conspiracy theorists were right. Hospital capacity wasn’t at breaking point. The truth was distorted.  

So what do you think—was it pure chance that Bill Gates invested heavily in BioNTech just two months before the world heard about a mysterious new virus?
